message.reasoning:
I will play Monopoly autonomously.

I am p4 with $106 cash and four unmortgaged properties. I just paid $450 rent to p2. p1 has $1086 and owns many utilities but no monopoly yet. I need to decide on my next move.

p2 holds a green monopoly with two houses on each property and mortgaged others. p3 has a dark blue monopoly with two houses on Park Place and three on Boardwalk, while the rest of their holdings are mortgaged. The bank still has Baltic, Oriental, Kentucky, and Atlantic unowned. I cannot trade New York Avenue because that would complete p1's orange monopoly.

I cannot trade States Avenue because that would complete p3's pink monopoly. Indiana blocks the red line, and Marvin blocks the yellow line. I have no monopoly yet, and my cash is low after paying rent and mortgaging Marvin. The green properties are too expensive to land on again, and the dark blue properties are impossible to survive.

Trading with p2 would give them a mortgaged property, so it is not worthwhile. I will mortgage one of my unmortgaged properties to raise cash.

Trading with p3 would complete their pink monopoly, but they would need to unmortgage States to build. That is too risky. I am calculating which spaces I could land on from Pennsylvania Avenue.

Rolling a 3 from Pennsylvania Avenue lands on Park Place, where p3 has two houses and charges $600 rent. That would drain my remaining cash.

Rolling a 3 or a 5 from Pennsylvania Avenue guarantees instant death. That is a one-in-six chance. I am checking mortgage values to raise enough cash to survive.

Mortgaging all three unmortgaged properties would raise cash to $386. That still cannot cover the $600 rent on Park Place or the $1400 rent on Boardwalk. I cannot survive the dark blue properties even with maximum cash.

Mortgaging now would only help against smaller hits, not the lethal dark blue squares. I can barely afford the $100 luxury tax with my current cash. The realistic options are either trading for more cash or breaking p3's monopoly by acquiring Park Place or Boardwalk, but they will not trade those properties.

I cannot bankrupt p3. The green properties are also lethal: Pacific and North Carolina charge $390 each, which I cannot afford with $106. I will not land on them again until I go around the board. Two opponents hold monopolies with houses, while I have no monopoly and only blockers.

Three houses on New York Avenue would cost $900 to build, making p1's orange monopoly lethal. Trading States for p3 would not immediately threaten me because their pink properties are mortgaged and cannot be built on.

Unmortgaging p3's pink properties would cost $165, which exceeds their $112 cash. I am now considering trading Indiana Avenue to p3, since they already own Illinois.

Trading Indiana for Illinois would not complete a monopoly, and p3 has only $112 cash. Selling the mortgaged Marvin Gardens to p2 is unlikely to help because the yellow line is still incomplete without Atlantic, and the buyer would pay mortgage interest to unmortgage it. I cannot trade States, Indiana, or Marvin to p1 because none of those properties would strengthen their position.

I cannot trade New York Avenue to p1 because they only want it. No opponent will break their green or dark blue monopolies for my single properties, since those monopolies are their win conditions. Trading away blockers for cash would accelerate my death. I will end my turn and hope.

Mortgaging States Avenue would raise cash to $176, Indiana to $216, and New York to $206. All three mortgaged together would yield $386. That buffer would cover the luxury tax, low railroad and utility rents, and some chance cards.

Oriental Avenue is exactly 12 spaces away, reachable with a roll of 12. Buying it would deny p1 their light blue monopoly. Baltic Avenue is only 9 spaces away, reachable with a roll of 9. Kentucky and Atlantic are too far to reach in one turn.

Baltic Avenue does not block a monopoly by itself, since the brown line requires both Mediterranean and Baltic. Mortgaging all three properties would still leave me unable to survive the lethal rolls of 3 and 5. Rolling a 4 would hit the luxury tax, which I can afford with my current cash. Rolling a 6 would land me on GO and collect $200.

Rolling 7 from Pennsylvania Avenue lands on Mediterranean, yielding $198 after passing GO and paying rent. Rolling 8 lands on Baltic, giving a net gain of $186 if purchased. Rolling 9 hits the income tax, leaving cash unchanged at $106. Rolling 10 reaches the mortgaged Reading Railroad for another $200. Rolling 11 lands on unowned Oriental, netting $100 if bought.

Oriental Avenue would deny p1 their light blue monopoly. Rolling a 6 passes GO and collects $200, the main cash infusion. The probability of dying on the next roll is 16.7 percent from rolls of 3 or 5.

I am now considering selling New York Avenue for about $700. That would leave me with roughly $806, enough to survive the $600 rent on Park Place but not the $1400 rent on Boardwalk. p1 would immediately build houses on their orange monopoly and could even afford three houses on St James Place.

Three houses on New York Avenue would cost $300. p1 could mortgage Short Line, Electric, and Water Works to raise roughly $250, giving them about $636 total. That would allow two houses on each orange property, yielding rents of $200 to $220. Demanding $800 would still leave them with enough cash to build five houses.

Selling New York Avenue would create a third deadly orange monopoly, so that trade is rejected. I am now checking whether properties with buildings can be traded.

I am uncertain whether the engine allows trading properties with buildings, since the schema only lists space keys. p3 has only $112 and will not trade Boardwalk. I am now considering offering p2 my mortgaged Marvin Gardens plus Indiana Avenue for cash.

The mortgaged Marvin Gardens is worth only fifty to one hundred dollars, so it cannot provide enough cash. p3 has only one hundred twelve dollars, and their mortgaged properties would not help me survive. I will end my turn.

I will keep my properties unmortgaged. The engine allows mortgaging during rent payment if I go bankrupt, so pre-mortgaging is unnecessary. Unmortgaged properties still collect rent from opponents who land on them.

Pre-mortgaging now would leave idle cash that does not earn rent. Unmortgaged properties are more valuable in trades. The only lethal rolls are 3 and 5, and the luxury tax is survivable with current cash.

I am now checking whether any trade offers a positive expected value. I could propose a bad offer to p1 and see if they reject it, since the engine will ask again if more post-turn actions remain legal.

I am now considering selling New York Avenue for $1000. p1 has $1086 and might accept that price, giving me $1106. I am calculating whether that maximum cash would be worth the property.

Selling New York Avenue for $1000 would leave me with roughly $506 after paying the $600 rent on Park Place. Boardwalk remains lethal at $1400, and I still lack a monopoly. The orange monopoly would also become another kill zone, so the trade is not worthwhile.

Selling New York Avenue for $1000 would leave me with roughly $506 after paying the $600 rent on Park Place. Boardwalk remains lethal at $1400, and I still lack a buildable monopoly. The orange monopoly would also become another kill zone, so the trade is not worthwhile.

I realized that p1 owns St James Place and Tennessee Avenue, while I own New York Avenue. Acquiring both would complete the orange monopoly for me. I am now considering offering them my mortgaged Marvin Gardens plus Indiana Avenue in exchange for those two properties.

p1 would never trade their orange properties for mine, since that would complete my monopoly instead of theirs. I have no other monopolies to offer in exchange. I am now checking whether p3 might trade their pink properties for States Avenue.
